nodes.description: Carrier tumors carry a median of about 243 exome variants against 16 in MBD4-proficient uveal melanoma, with 85-96% of single-nucleotide variants being CpG>TpG transitions against about a quarter in other uveal melanomas. The excess continues after dissemination: metastases from MBD4-deficient tumors are genetically heterogeneous and acquire new drivers (TP53, SMARCA4, GNAS), whereas MBD4-proficient metastases acquire few new variants. How the mutator contributes to malignant transformation, beyond accompanying it, has not been determined (see discussions).

nodes.description: One constitutional MBD4 allele carries a truncating, canonical-splice or catalytically dead missense variant. Every cell keeps one functional allele, so the constitutional state is not itself a mutator state; it is a first hit awaiting loss of the wild-type allele in a uveal melanocyte. Recurrent alleles across unrelated carriers (c.1562-1G>T, c.1443delT, c.1706G>A, c.335+1G>A, c.939dup) suggest founder effects.

nodes.description: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy or anti-PD-1 with anti-CTLA-4 for metastatic disease. In unselected metastatic uveal melanoma, response rates are below 5%; in MBD4-deficient tumors, a retrospective series of 12 patients (most of them germline carriers, some with somatic MBD4 loss only) reported a 50% response rate, and in a 300-patient retrospective cohort 3 of 5 MBD4-mutated patients responded against 4% of wild-type. The evidence is retrospective and rests on small numbers, and how checkpoint blockade should be sequenced with tebentafusp in HLA-A*02:01-positive carriers is unresolved.

nodes.description: Constitutional Mbd4-null mice. They model the tumor-cell state of a carrier's uveal melanoma (both alleles lost), not the heterozygous germline state, and no uveal or melanocytic phenotype is reported.

In every sequenced tumor from a carrier, the wild-type MBD4 allele (3q21.3) was lost by monosomy 3 or isodisomy 3. Because BAP1 (3p21) lies on the same chromosome, the same event removes the wild-type BAP1 allele, and the carrier tumors with available profiles also carried somatic BAP1 inactivation. MBD4 deficiency in uveal melanoma is therefore tied to monosomy-3, high-metastatic-risk tumors.

nodes.description: The defining tumor. Primary uveal melanoma in carriers has been unilateral and single in nearly all reported cases, with one carrier with multiple uveal melanomas among 25 French carrier families. Carrier tumors are monosomy-3, hypermutated, and in the first series had metastasis-free and overall survival not different from MBD4-proficient monosomy-3 tumors. Median age at diagnosis was 55.5 years in the first eight carriers, not earlier than in non-carriers, and the discovery authors' model places the rate-limiting first step (a Gq-pathway activating mutation) upstream of any MBD4 effect, which they offer as the reason onset is not shifted earlier. No pediatric case was found in the sources cited here.
